topic: Change of state and latent heat

Teach: Radiation as heat transfer without a medium, electromagnetic wave nature of thermal radiation, emissivity and absorptivity of surfaces, distinction from conduction and convection | Do NOT teach: Stefan's law quantitative derivation, Wien's law derivation, Planck's quantum theory of radiation | Already covered: Heat transfer - conduction (c11_phy_069), Heat transfer - convection (c11_phy_070)

Teach: Blackbody concept (ideal/cavity radiator), Stefan-Boltzmann law I = sigmaT^4, emissivity in, radiant intensity, dimensions and SI unit of sigma | Do NOT teach: Deductions from Stefan's law, Planck's radiation law, spectral distribution derivation | Already covered: Heat transfer - radiation (c11_phy_071)

Teach: Newton's law of cooling dT/dt = -k(T - T_s), cooling curve interpretation, numerical problems on cooling, relationship to Stefan's law for small DeltaT | Do NOT teach: Deductions from Stefan's law, detailed heat transfer coefficient analysis, forced convection cooling | Already covered: Blackbody radiation and Stefan's law (c11_phy_073)

Teach: Thermal equilibrium concept, zeroth law of thermodynamics, temperature definition via equilibrium, distinction between heat work and internal energy | Do NOT teach: First law of thermodynamics, second law, thermodynamic processes, entropy | Already covered: Specific heat capacity and calorimetry (c11_phy_067)

topic: First law of thermodynamics (Q = DeltaU + W)

Teach: Adiabatic process definition (Q = 0, DeltaU = -W), PV^gamma = constant, PV graph comparison with isothermal, cooling on expansion and heating on compression | Do NOT teach: Derivation of PV^gamma = constant, work done formula W = (P_1V_1 - P_2V_2)/(gamma-1), Carnot cycle | Already covered: Isothermal process (c11_phy_078), First law of thermodynamics (c11_phy_077)

Teach: Derivation of isothermal work W = nRT ln(V_2/V_1) from PV = constant, work as area under PV graph, numerical problems on isothermal work, Cp and Cv relation Cp - Cv = R | Do NOT teach: Adiabatic work derivation, derivation of PV^gamma = constant, detailed kinetic theory derivation of Cp - Cv = R | Already covered: Isothermal process (c11_phy_078), First law of thermodynamics (c11_phy_077)

Teach: Work done in adiabatic process W = (P_1V_1 - P_2V_2)/(gamma-1), relation Cp - Cv = R, work as area under PV graph | Do NOT teach: Derivation of PV^gamma = constant | Already covered: Isothermal and adiabatic process definitions (c11_phy_078, c11_phy_079)

Teach: Second law of thermodynamics (Kelvin's and Clausius' statements), reversible and irreversible processes, heat engine concept | Do NOT teach: Entropy as a quantitative concept, statistical formulation of Second Law | Already covered: First law of thermodynamics (c11_phy_077)

Teach: Carnot cycle (four stages on PV diagram), efficiency formula eta = 1 - T_2/T_1, numerical problems | Do NOT teach: Derivation of Carnot efficiency, real engine cycles (Otto, Diesel) | Already covered: Second law of thermodynamics (c11_phy_082); Isothermal and adiabatic processes (c11_phy_078, c11_phy_079)

Teach: Infrasonic frequencies (below 20 Hz) and their applications; Difference between infrasonic and subsonic | Do NOT teach: Detailed seismology; Infrasonic monitoring technology; C10: Wave properties of infrasound | Already covered: C6: Pitch depends on frequency; C9: Nature of sound waves and V = flambda

Teach: Sonic (audible) frequencies (20-20,000 Hz) as the human hearing range | Do NOT teach: Detailed anatomy of the ear; Audiometry and hearing loss; C10: Sound intensity in decibels | Already covered: C6: Pitch depends on frequency; C9: Nature of sound waves and V = flambda

Teach: Ultrasonic frequencies (above 20,000 Hz) and their applications (sonar, medical imaging, detection); Difference between ultrasonic and supersonic | Do NOT teach: Detailed sonar equations; Medical ultrasound physics and piezoelectric effect; C10: Acoustic impedance and reflection coefficients | Already covered: C6: Pitch depends on frequency; C9: Nature of sound waves and V = flambda

Teach: Concept of free electrons; Types of conductors (good, bad, semiconductors, superconductors); Electric charge Q and its SI unit; Quantum nature of charge (Q = ne); Direction of flow of charge | Do NOT teach: Detailed band theory of semiconductors; C10: Electric fields and Gauss's law; C11: Capacitance and dielectrics | Already covered: C8: Static electricity and charge by friction; C7: Basic electric circuit (cell, bulb, switch)

topic: Electric current as rate of flow of charge
scope: Teach: Electric current as rate of flow of charge (I = Q/t); Conventional vs electronic direction of current; Elementary idea of work done in transferring charge; Detection of current by galvanometer or ammeter | Do NOT teach: Detailed internal working of galvanometer; C10: Kirchhoff's laws and complex circuit analysis; C11: Drift velocity and mobility | Already covered: C7: Electric current as flow of charge (qualitative); C8: Static electricity and charge by friction

Teach: Potential difference V = W/Q (no derivation); SI unit (volt); Concept of resistance and its SI unit (ohm); Circuit symbols; Electric circuit using cell, key, resistance wire/rheostat; Brief introduction to sources of direct current (cells, accumulators) | Do NOT teach: Construction, working and equations of cells and accumulators; Derivation of V = W/Q; C10: EMF and internal resistance; C11: Wheatstone bridge and potentiometer | Already covered: C7: Potential difference and voltage (qualitative); C9: Electric current as I = Q/t

Teach: Ohm's law (V = IR), concept of resistance and its SI unit, simple numerical problems | Do NOT teach: Series and parallel combinations of resistors; Internal resistance of cells; Kirchhoff's laws | Already covered: Electric current as rate of flow of charge; Potential difference (V = W/q)

Teach: Standard circuit symbols, circuit diagrams with cells and resistors, detection of current by galvanometer/ammeter, sources of direct current | Do NOT teach: Construction, working and equations of cells and accumulators; Complex multi-loop circuits | Already covered: Ohm's law (V = IR); Electric current and potential difference

Teach: Induced magnetism by bar magnets, induction precedes attraction, magnetic materials vs non-magnetic materials | Do NOT teach: Electromagnetic induction (Faraday's law); Electromagnets and their construction; Magnetic flux and flux density | Already covered: Magnetic effect of electric current; Magnets have poles and attract/repel

topic: Earth's magnetic field and neutral points
scope: Teach: Earth's magnetic field and its evidence, magnetic compass, neutral points, properties of magnetic field lines, uniform vs non-uniform fields | Do NOT teach: Geomagnetic reversals; Magnetosphere and Van Allen belts; Electromagnetic induction | Already covered: Induced magnetism; Magnets have poles and attract/repel; Magnetic compass finds directions

topic: Work, energy and machine efficiency - work-energy principle
scope: Teach: Work formula, KE and PE, efficiency, energy conservation in machines | Do NOT teach (reserved for later): C10: Mechanical advantage (MA = L/E); C10: Velocity ratio (VR = dE/dL); C10: Efficiency of machines (eta = MA/VR) | Already covered (revise only, don't re-teach): C7: Machines and mechanical advantage - introduction to MA concept

Teach: Torque, lever equilibrium, VR for levers | Do NOT teach (reserved for later): C10: Levers (classes I, II, III with MA and VR - detailed numerical problems) | Already covered (revise only, don't re-teach): C7: Levers - mechanical advantage and classes

topic: Elasticity and deformation of solids - stress and strain (introduction)
scope: Teach: Elasticity, stress/strain (qualitative), Hooke's law (qualitative) | Do NOT teach (reserved for later): C11: Hooke's law and Young's modulus (quantitative, modulus calculation) | Already covered (revise only, don't re-teach): C7: Solid state - properties and particle arrangement

topic: Surface tension and capillary action - introduction (qualitative)
scope: Teach: Surface tension (qualitative), capillary action, factors affecting surface tension | Do NOT teach (reserved for later): C11: Surface tension (quantitative, force calculation); C11: Capillary rise (Jurin's law, height calculation) | Already covered (revise only, don't re-teach): C7: Liquid state - properties and particle arrangement
